semantics.clock: State changes on rising clk edges; sensor values are sampled at those edges, as implied by the requested synchronous state machine.
semantics.reset: Active-high synchronous reset takes priority and establishes lowest level with all four outputs asserted, explicitly required by original text.
semantics.levels: 000 lowest, 001 lower middle, 011 upper middle, 111 highest; nominal fr2:fr0 respectively 111, 011, 001, 000, from original table.
semantics.supplemental: At an intermediate level, set dfr if previous distinct sampled level was lower; clear if it was higher; retain across repeated samples. Original text explicitly says previous lower than current opens the supplemental valve.
semantics.extremes: Lowest level forces dfr=1; highest forces dfr=0 as maximum and zero flow require.
semantics.initialization: No power-up value specified; state is uninitialized until reset or a determining sensor transition. Verification starts with a synchronous reset.

numeric.arithmetic: Only ordinal comparisons; no overflow or signed operations

verification.oracle: Independent integer water-level history and table derived from original problem
verification.cases: Synchronous reset priority and timing, all 16 ordered valid level transitions, repeated levels, rise/fall history, skipped levels, exhaustive length-four sequences
verification.sampling: Inputs change on falling edges; check output stability before next rising edge and correctness after rising edge NBA updates
verification.completion: Fatal mismatches, bounded timeout, PASS line only after all checks

specification_ambiguities.resolution: Hold state on patterns other than 000,001,011,111; no correctness claims for invalid patterns
Use rising edge for the synchronous state machine
Do not add initialization; verify only after synchronous reset

specification_ambiguities.issue: Skipped sensor levels not separately described
specification_ambiguities.resolution: Compare previous distinct sampled rank with current rank, following the stated previous-level rule
